subject: botany_2
question_text: What are porins? What role do they play in diffusion?

verification.note: Sourced from "Sr. Botany — My Baby Bullet-Q" (Sri Publishers, STAR-Q Pass Track), book p.38, printed question 49. Botany-II holds only ONE source book: the TSBIE Basic Learning Material in hand covers physics only, and no Telangana Botany-II board paper is in the corpus, so the two-book union check and the board back-test are BOTH structurally impossible for this card — "not checked" does NOT mean "checked and clean". Run both the moment a second source or a real paper arrives. The mark split is a claim until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it. Revised 2026-09-05 after the examiner audit: the s2 line and why no longer call the movement simple diffusion or set diffusion against transport, since NCERT places porins in the facilitated diffusion section and facilitated diffusion is itself passive transport; the wording now says only that the movement is passive and follows the concentration gradient, which is safe under either name.

insider_note: Two halves, one mark each. The second half must say 'without using energy' or the answer reads as active transport.

steps.margin_note: Two lines: what they are made of, and where they sit.
lines: Porins are proteins that form large pores in
They are found in the outer membranes of
steps.why: Naming them as pore-forming proteins is what separates them from carrier proteins, which move one molecule at a time.
common_mistakes: Calling porins a kind of lipid. They are PROTEINS.
Saying they are found in every membrane. They sit in OUTER membranes of plastids, mitochondria and some bacteria.
steps.memory_tip: Porin makes a pore: the name is the structure.

steps.label: Their role in diffusion
steps.margin_note: Say what fits through and say no energy is used. Both halves of the mark.

lines.text: A big open pore, so no energy is needed

lines: The pore is large enough to let even small
Molecules move through the pore passively,
down the concentration gradient, without using
steps.why: The pore is permanently open, so nothing has to be pumped and no ATP is spent — the movement is passive and follows the concentration gradient.
common_mistakes: Saying porins pump molecules across. Nothing is pumped; molecules DIFFUSE through.
Leaving out the size. The point of a porin is that even small proteins fit.
steps.memory_tip: A hole does not push; things fall through it on their own.
